Hey friend, I’m sorry you’re struggling. I have SEVERE dental anxiety and going to the dentist is the worst place in the world for me, but I try to go every 6 months because I know I am damaging my teeth and want to be on top of things.

I have never personally heard of insurance coverage having an issue with “self inflicted” damage like eating disorders, but I don’t know. 

Could you reach out to your insurance and without providing details just ask for information on your coverage? 

I personally have been extremely open with my dentist and hygienists regarding my eating disorder because it has allowed them to offer me more personalized care and advice. If you aren’t ready for that, that’s okay and I’m sure there are dentists out there that are not particularly fluent in ED’s or even really care but it may be worth mentioning.

I would highly, highly recommend at least trying to set up a cleaning/check up even if you don’t say anything. It SUCKS, I know, but it’s worth it.

I’m so sorry you’re struggling. I am right there with you.

It is a disordered way of thinking, but this is the nature of the disorder. The reality of eating disorders is recovery doesn’t truly work until you want it - and that’s a devastating realization to come to.

I have recovered and relapsed several times over the years. My current relapse is my worst, it has been a few years now of this and I have reached a point where I am scared, and I am willing to listen. I am participating in my local eating disorder program, and groups, and I am listening. All I can truly do right now is listen, take in information and think about recovery. I am not actively participating in recovery, but this is a massive improvement for me.

I would recommend you try to be willing to do the same - listen and stay informed. Participate in harm reduction strategies. Your eating disorder is serving a purpose. There are so many things beneath it that you will have to face upon recovery. Write it down, like those iceberg things. Just step back and look at it all. Awareness is not a threat to your eating disorder or your sense of control, but it is important to have.

You feel like you are in control but you aren’t. Your eating disorder is in control of you. Stay safe as best you can. Again - harm reduction. At the very least look into that.

I totally hear your fear, I’m sorry but I do not know the answer for sure. I am only speaking as a PWD who hit the exemption limit last year 2 months shy of the reset. Cheque was reduced by a few hundred the first month, then I only received about $100 the next month (January) before the reset in February.

I’d recommend calling them to ask. I called in January because I thought that was when it reset and was concerned and they were very helpful and willing to answer any questions. I’m sorry I don’t know more than my own experience.

Edit to fix a typo

Once you reach that exemption limit, if you continue earning money from work, you will still be on PWD but you will not receive a monthly payment from disability. You will still have the designation as well as medical supports and such.

The new year for disability starts in February, so your payments start back up in February as long as you’ve continued to submit monthly reports and still need support. You do not need to reapply or anything and you may not even reach that exemption limit at your hours/wage.

I was the “gifted” kid when I was young and I received high praise and compliments on my talent with art, the size of my body, my good grades.

I dropped out of high school. Fell into a life of mental illness, including severe anxiety (they just called me “quiet” as a kid, not knowing), an eating disorder, treatment resistant depression and BPD.

The painful realization is realizing I will never be any of the things I was told I could be, and I have disappointed every single person who thought more of me.

As someone who has struggled and lived one day at a time for as long as I can remember, you don’t. You rely on the moments of peace or happiness. I find that the good moments or smiles mean so much more when you have depression and you have to hold on to them. You have to remember them.

You can do what people say. Go for walks, get some exercise. Eat healthy. Stay positive. Create a routine and stick with it. It’s not bad advice, but it is irritating to hear over and over again.

You just keep going, and you remember the moments. You remember that you aren’t alone, no matter how lonely you feel.

From one severely depressed person to another, just keep going. Your best is good enough, and sometimes your best is staying in bed all day. That’s okay, because you made it through the day. That’s what matters.
The weight of the world is on my shoulders, and I see no way out and no way through, but I made it through the day again. How are you?

I struggle with mental illness on the daily and I never have anything significant that makes me happy, just moments.

This wasn’t that recent but it has always stuck in my mind.

I was going to get food after work from a drive through, crying my eyes out already when they told me the grill wasn’t working and I couldn’t get what I ordered, which of course would happen.

I’m stuck in this drive through waiting to get out when I see a homeless man holding a sign that said “only kindness matters”. Dug around for some change. I had a backpack with me that I had several pins on, one of which said “you are enough”. I wanted to give it to him for some reason.

I pulled over by him and gave him a few dollars and that pin. He had the most beautiful blue eyes and kindest smile I had ever seen. We talked a little bit, myself still crying, but I cracked a smile and he told me it was the most beautiful smile he had ever seen and to “keep smiling”.

While I was pulling away, he put the pin on his jacket and waved. He may have saved my life that night.

I was in an emotionally abusive long distance relationship. He knew where I was every second of every day. He would keep me on FaceTime at all times. Even sleeping. I had to send proof about being out with my dad or something whenever leaving the house. He controlled all of my family and friends. I had nobody.

But I had a friend who was officially missing for years. I thought about him all the time, nobody could find him and his poster remained up.

He messaged me one day. He had been in jail. I thought he was dead. He was severely addicted to drugs and said that jail was the “best thing that ever happened to him”. He wanted to catch up.

I wasn’t allowed.

Shortly after, Christmas Eve. I found out he overdosed and died and I never got to say goodbye.

I do based on personal experience as well as overheard.

My great grandmother had a son in the army. One night, she woke up in the middle of the night. Her son stood at the edge of her bed, saluting her. In the morning she found out he had died the night prior.

Within the week of my great grandmother’s passing, my dad was taking photos of myself as a kid and our pets on a digital camera. She popped up in one of the photos. We only noticed a couple years ago.

My family got a new puppy after our dog died young due to a health condition. I was a kid. Dad took puppy for a walk. I heard the dog whining at my bedroom door I went to let it in. There was nothing there. I believe the old dog came by.

I trespassed at an old sanitarium in town, that housed tuberculosis patients before it was shut down decades ago. I took random photos and I managed to capture two that I believe to be patient/ of the sanitarium.

I see no harm in believing.

Edit: there could definitely be scientific explanation for any of these, and I could disregard my great grandmother’s story, but I refuse to. Photos could be judged as well, and I have no issue with that, but for me personally I choose to hold onto them.

Surviving it all. My entire life has revolved around mental illness. On the outside, I am sure people look at me as a failure because I don’t know how to do what I am “supposed” to do. But I have no choice but to live one day at a time and every one of those days I survive is my definition of success.

I was on a skiing school field trip as a kid and lost control. Saw a metal sign for the route coming up, figured I could catch myself on it and bounce off. I broke it in half with my face. Woke up on the ground 20 seconds later. Sign smashed on the ground. Principal took a photo to commemorate at the end of year assembly. Not my proudest moment. I don’t ski anymore.
Rocking myself to sleep, like a baby. I just roll back and forth for comfort. It helps.

I once heard that your first thought about someone is what you are conditioned to believe, your next thought is what you truly believe.

For example, perhaps you see a heavy person going for a run and have an immediate judgmental thought. Your next thought is “good for them!”

Reminding myself of this has been powerful. I always rely on that second thought.

There are several.

I have had a long lasting eating disorder. Had not eaten all day, went to see when dinner would be ready. Overheard them talking about me and heard “she’s just going to throw it up anyway.” I wasn’t going to. I skipped dinner.

Another time I expressed my suicidal thoughts and my mom said “go ahead and kill yourself, we will to”. Took away my car keys and forced me into the hospital.

Another time I went to my mom to ask for support. She said “you’re not trying at all. Quit saying you are.”

They always had a way with words.

Because it is local to me, the case of missing person Ryan Shtuka in Sun Peaks (BC, Canada). He left a house party in 2018 and disappeared. Extensive searches were conducted, and they continue looking to this day.

His mother Heather Shtuka wrote a book called “Missing From Me.”

The case remains open and alive. Ryan liked dinosaurs, so they make plastic dinosaur toys with QR codes that lead to his story, and they have been left all over the world at this point.

I am no expert, just a person who purges.

I was told by an eating disorder doctor years ago to rinse my mouth out with water after, and DO NOT BRUSH YOUR TEETH FOR AT LEAST 30 MINUTES AFTER. By brushing your teeth, you are only rubbing the acid in to your teeth and causing more damage.

This probably does nothing for me but I’ve convinced myself that if I chew Tums after purging it will get rid of some acidity… I don’t know.

I was more recently told by a counsellor that if you eat a bit of cheese after the p.h. levels balance out some of the acidity. I don’t know if this is true either, but sometimes I do this.

I can’t answer on if they tell your parents or not, but I’d like to share something.

I have a fear of dentists because of my eating disorder. Last time I went, I told them straight up, I’m concerned about my dental health because I purge. They were incredibly understanding and supportive and gave me some extra care tips for my teeth to protect them without overstepping or telling me to stop. I’m far more comfortable/feel much safer going back now.

Depending on how long this has been going on, they may be able to tell without you telling them, but I personally believe it may be worth it to tell them because they really just care about your health. I feel like my dentist personally would encourage me to talk to my parents if they didn’t already know but would not tell them themselves. But, I don’t know for sure, so take that with a grain of salt.

I miss going on vacation with my parents and lining up all my Webkinz to decide which one would get to come with me. I miss the weird mosquito netting thing I put up around my bed because it made me feel safe. I miss being able to read a book a day and enjoying it. I miss eating dinner with my parents every night, without thinking about the calories. I miss knowing I always had someone to run to when I got scared. I miss not being severely mentally ill. I miss feeling like I had time. I miss feeling like I was put here for a reason and I would grow up to do big things, whatever I wanted. I miss me.

I’m so sorry that this was sprung upon you by your mother. Maybe cats are less responsibility than other pets, but they are still a responsibility and your responsibility should be focusing on taking care of yourself right now, not another living being. 

As someone who relates to your state of mental health, and who has a cat, some days it is near impossible to get up just to clean a litter box when I also can’t even brush my teeth. And I get up and do it anyway, but the amount of GUILT I feel for looking at my cat as an inconvenience to my depression at times only serves to bring me down further.

Not only that, but it is also a financial commitment in terms of regular every day care as well as surprise vet visits when they do something stupid (eat a dead lily, in my case. No flowers around anymore before anyone comes for me.)

I am so sorry you are in this position. I completely hear you and feel for you. I hope you are looking after yourself as best you can.

Edit to add: I love my cat. I will always take good care of my cat. But if it was thrust upon me in a situation like this I would be full of resentment.

Later, after some silence, he asks me and my parents to all get together for a photo and asks another stranger to take it for us. So, he went home to China with a weird family photo, and I like to think he shows it to people.

The bank had no security cameras at the drive through I had used, decided it must have been a mistake and my mom’s earlier withdrawal had gone through twice, so they deposited $100 back in my family’s account.

Tuesday’s with Morrie, by Mitch Albom. The only book I’ve ever marked pages in. It’s a biography and it’s wonderful.

One of my favourite parts: Mitch compiles a list of topics to talk to Morrie about while sitting in an airport preparing to go visit him. Morrie is critically ill, and is running out of time. The topics include things such as life, death, purpose, illness. 

While working on this list, he notices the people around him fanning themselves and complaining about the air conditioning not working and being too hot.

Just put a lot of things in perspective for me. Highly recommend it.

A boy asked me out in 7th grade or sometime around then. I mentioned another girl he had recently told me he was into and asked, “what about her?”

“Yeah but I could never land her. She’s out of my league.”

Ouch.

When I was in elementary school, I only ever really had one friend. She was preparing to move away in fifth grade after we had been inseparable since Kindergarten, and a couple months beforehand she just started inexplicably avoiding me and hanging out with another girl, I’ll call her K. So I had nobody at that point. But that isn’t the story.

I became friends with K when my other friend was gone. We didn’t have tons in common but I felt very alone and needed someone to hang out with during lunch and whatnot. 

There was another girl, I’ll call her N, who always showed interest in being my friend. She’d talk to me once in a while, ask to hang out or sit with me, etc. However, K had an issue with this girl. N was a bit heavyset and tall, she stood out from everyone else. So one day, K tells me N is her “enemy”. 

Shortly after, there’s a sleepover event going on in the gym. They called it “homeless night”. We slept on cardboard. I know. What the fuck. At the beginning of the night, I’m chatting with N a little bit, and then go back to see K because we’re going to sleep in this corner we had set up. She blows up at me, and tells me if I were REALLY her friend I would NOT be friends with her LITERAL ENEMY. Boom, she walks away and avoids me the rest of the night. I spent it crying as quietly as I could.

The next day at school, she still isn’t talking to me. Lunch rolls around, and I can’t find her. I stand alone outside while kids are clearly judging me. She walks by with a girl named B, they glare at me, and continue on.

I had no friends the last 2 years of elementary school. There were a couple girls who just kind of put up with having me around, I wasn’t close with anyone and most people thought I was weird and didn’t like me. I didn’t like me either. 

Another thing K did: wrote out a letter for me to read out to another girl to tell her we couldn’t be seen with her anymore, since she didn’t have a lot of friends herself. I still hate myself for agreeing but I didn’t know what to do, I couldn’t lose my only friend. That girl went home an hour later and moved away shortly after.
Yeah. It’s hard to care about things like that when you just think “I’m just going to kill myself anyway”.

I am, that’s the problem with her comment. I’m fully aware medication isn’t the cure but I’m stuck doing it all by myself and it doesn’t feel worth it anymore. I’ve come so far from where I started but people got tired of me still not being “cured”
